title: Showcase: the obstacle course run
summary: Set up the shoebox course, run it once for the family, and explain one line of code and one bug from the sprint, told proudly.
materials: mBot's battery, charged, or 4 AA batteries
tape measure for the physics extra

figure.alt: A top-down shoebox course: mBot starts at one side, a dashed path weaves between four scattered shoeboxes to a finish point. Text below notes one run with one retry if stuck, and explaining one line of code plus one bug.

items.s: one run, one retry if stuck
explain one code line + tell one bug

steps.title: Run the course
steps.body:
Set up the same kind of shoebox course you built in week 7. Scatter four to six boxes so the robot actually has to notice something and turn.

Run the demo:

1. Run the course live for the family, one run, start to finish.
2. If mBot gets stuck or slams into a box, stop and put it back at the start.
3. Try again once, one retry only.
4. Explain one line of code from the program, in your own words, and why it is there.
5. Tell the family one bug from the whole build sprint, the one that gave you the most trouble.
6. Say what you expected, what actually happened, and the step that showed you where the bug was hiding.

Tell the bug proudly, like a scientist reporting a real finding, not like an apology. A real demo sometimes fails once and still finishes.

steps.title: Show it
steps.prompt: A photo of your course set up before the run, or a short video of the whole run, retry included if it happens.

extras.title: Time the run and try to beat it
extras.body:
Add a real number to your demo instead of just pass or fail.

1. Before the family watches, time one practice run through the course, start to finish.
2. Write that number down as your first time.
3. Run the timed demo for the family, timing it the same way.
4. If you get your one allowed retry, time that run too.
5. Say both numbers out loud to the family.

What to notice: a faster time does not always mean fewer bumps along the way.

extras.title: Add one new trick to the course run
extras.body:
What would make this obstacle course run more impressive to watch?

Add exactly one new behaviour to the obstacle avoider code from week 7.

It must add exactly one new behaviour to the code from week 7.
It must have one number you choose by testing, like a cutoff or a sound.
It must be shown running the real course to someone in your house first.

Sketch your idea first.

How to know it works: your new trick happens the same way on two runs in a row.

extras.title: How far does mBot really travel per turn?
extras.body:
Find out how many centimeters mBot actually travels for a fixed number of wheel turns you command in code.

1. Predict first: guess how many centimeters mBot will travel when you command its wheels to turn exactly 5 rotations. Write your number in the Maker's Log.
2. Mark a starting line on the floor with tape.
3. Program mBot to drive forward exactly 5 wheel rotations, then stop.
4. Run it from the starting line and mark where it stops.
5. Measure the distance between the two marks with a tape measure.

Compare: was your prediction close to the measured distance, longer, or shorter?

Teach it: tell a grown-up in two sentences why the same number of wheel turns always covers about the same distance.

extras.title: Rewrite your best log
extras.body:
Your logs are the writing you do here, and writing gets better by rewriting, not by more of it. Pick your best log from this sprint and rewrite it once.

1. Read the log out loud. Mark every sentence that tries to say two things.
2. Rewrite so each sentence carries one idea. Split, do not shorten.
3. Find every adjective (hard, cool, weird) and replace it with a number or a fact: how many tries, how long, what broke.
4. Put the reason before the claim: "the loop ran twice, so the heart flashed twice" rather than "the heart flashed twice, because the loop ran twice".
5. Read both versions to someone and ask which one they could follow without you in the room.

What to notice: the rewrite is usually shorter and says more. That is the whole trick.
